one_liner: Lean-verified peephole optimizer for Skia command streams; 1.12x geomean raster speedup over Skia Graphite on Chrome-generated pictures.
what_it_does: The OOPSLA 2026 paper defines muSkia, a three-strata formal semantics of the Skia 2D API (canvas state, layer stack, clips, blending, colour filters), mechanized in Lean 4 in under a thousand lines. It uses that semantics to prove four rewrites of wasteful command patterns that Chrome emits, then implements them as an optimizer inside a Skia fork. The optimizer edits a recorded SkRecord (the in-memory form of an .skp picture) in place before playback. It is a pre-pass in front of Skia, not a rasterizer, and it only helps clients that record pictures before drawing them.
how_it_is_fast: It removes or cheapens SaveLayer/Restore pairs, each of which costs an offscreen GPU surface plus a blend. The four rewrites are: drop opaque SrcOver SaveLayers that contain only SrcOver draws; turn a DstIn mask layer into a Clip; fold a luminance or colour filter into the draws it covers; and delete opaque gradient masks used by one Russian web framework (mail.ru, dzen.ru, yandex.ru). Each rewrite is a single linear pass driven by a stack of small state machines, one per open SaveLayer (SkOptPass<MatchState>, with an inline STArray<8> frame stack). Removed commands become NoOps, and insertions are buffered and merged in one scan, a technique the paper credits to WebKit B3's InsertionSet. Optimization took at most 0.03 ms per picture on the M2.
when_to_use: Skia clients that record SkPictures/SkRecords before playback (browser engines, compositors, picture-replay tools) and whose command streams nest SaveLayers for opacity, masks or filters.

Web-content rendering where Chrome-style output uses SrcOver or DstIn layers for clipping and masking: the paper's largest gains were 3.04x on a vimeo.com layer (three rewrites chained) and 2.41x on dzen.ru (gradient-mask rewrite).
Research or tooling that needs a machine-checked definition of Skia's layer, blend and clip semantics to prove a draw-list rewrite correct before shipping it.
GPU backends, Graphite in particular: measured gains were higher there (1.12x on Apple M2 Metal, 1.14x on an Intel CoffeeLake-S GT2 integrated GPU) than on legacy Ganesh (1.08x and 1.07x).
when_not_to_use: As a faster rasterizer: it does not touch Skia's path filling, shaders or GPU pipeline, so pictures without SaveLayers gain nothing and pay the optimizer pass (the RQ3 total-time CDF shows more slowdowns for exactly those).

Pixel-exact pipelines: the rewrites are proved over real-valued colours, so anti-aliasing and rounding may change. 25 of 139 benchmark pictures had pixels differing by more than 1% in a channel (judged anti-aliasing by eye).

Programs that use mask filters, blurs, image filters, SkSL shaders or bitmap features: muSkia does not formalize these, the passes give up on unmodelled commands, and only 41 of 139 pictures could be converted for translation validation.

Legacy Ganesh with complex clip paths: the DstIn-to-Clip rewrite slowed avast.com layer 0 significantly on Ganesh/Intel; Graphite/Intel showed three statistically significant slowdowns (intuit.com layer 15, two gravatar.com layers).

Production use today: the code is a research fork of Skia (commit f931a2e, between milestones 143 and 144) shipped only as a Zenodo artifact, and per the first author Chrome and Skia had not agreed to upstream it as of June 2026.

integration.form: source-drop (patches in a research fork of Skia; Lean 4 proofs as a separate artifact)
integration.dependencies: Skia at commit f931a2e; Lean 4 for the semantics and translation validator; Python playwright scripts to capture .skp files from Chrome
integration.min_toolchain: Built with Clang 17.0.0 (-O3 -flto=thin) on macOS and Clang 18.1.3 on Ubuntu 24.04.4 in the paper; a minimum is not documented
integration.platforms: Backend-agnostic, since it rewrites SkRecords before playback; evaluated on Graphite/Metal and Ganesh/OpenGL on an Apple M2, and on Graphite and Ganesh on Intel i7-8700K with CoffeeLake-S GT2 graphics
integration.thread_safety: not documented (mutates an SkRecord in place)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it runs on Skia's own SkRecord type in front of unchanged backends, but only inside the authors' Skia fork, and it applies only to recorded pictures, not immediate-mode SkCanvas calls

gotchas: The catalogued 18.7% (99 programs, 32 us) is the March 2026 arXiv v1 abstract. The camera-ready paper re-ran with 25 nanobench runs per picture and reports a 1.12x geomean on 139 pictures, at most 0.03 ms to optimize, and up to 3.04x.

The benchmark set keeps only Chrome layer pictures that contain SaveLayer. Only 51 of the 139 are rewritten at all, and 38 of those have 95% confidence intervals entirely above 1x. The geomean includes unrewritten pictures whose ratios (0.96x-1.09x) are noise.

The numbers are per-layer .skp playback times in Skia's nanobench, with the optimization applied offline. They are not whole-page frame times inside Chrome, and Chrome's layer split differs by hardware, so each machine got its own capture.

The SrcOver-SaveLayer rewrite requires the layer to be opaque, a side condition the Lean model tracks but the paper's simplified rules omit; removing a layer can also defeat Graphite's own first-draw clear optimization (intuit.com regression).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only when you are already on Skia and want fewer offscreen layers in recorded pictures without changing the rasterizer. Blend2D, ThorVG or Vello CPU replace the rasterizer and are the siblings to look at if raw fill speed is the problem, and the two approaches can stack.
verified_claims_summary: Peer-reviewed first-party measurement (PACMPL OOPSLA2 2026, article 339), read from the camera-ready LaTeX in the first author's public skia-paper repo. On an 8-core Apple M2 (16 GB) with Skia f931a2e built by Clang 17.0.0 -O3 -flto=thin, Graphite/Metal nanobench playback of 139 SaveLayer-bearing pictures from Chrome on the top 100 sites (median of 25 runs, bootstrap 95% CI) gives a 1.12x geomean (max 3.04x). The other runs: Ganesh on the M2 1.08x; Intel i7-8700K with CoffeeLake-S GT2 (Clang 18.1.3) 1.14x Graphite and 1.07x Ganesh on 143 recaptured pictures; the next 100 sites 1.18x on 144 pictures with the passes frozen.
status_note: Research artifact (Zenodo record 21386615, not opened here because zenodo is blocked) accepted at OOPSLA 2026; no public GitHub repository for the Skia fork or the Lean code was found, and it is not upstreamed in Skia or Chrome, so treat it as a reference design rather than a library.
